meta.verdict_note: This is a pre-bid review: your home measured straight off your drawings, plus the scope to make sure any bid you get actually covers. Bring it to the table before you sign.

findings.title: Site work, driveway & final grading
findings.detail: Grading, the driveway, and the final grade are the single most common thing a bid under-carries or buries in a vague "site allowance." It lands late, and it is rarely small.
findings.basis: Standard scope for a build like yours -- confirm your bid addresses it.

findings.title: Gutters & downspouts
findings.detail: A small line that goes missing from bids more than almost any other. It never gets cheaper after the paint is on.
findings.basis: Standard scope for a build like yours -- confirm your bid addresses it.

findings.title: Home technology, security & low-voltage
findings.detail: Structured wiring, cameras, alarm, and automation are frequently left out and come back as a five-figure change order mid-build, when your leverage is gone.
findings.basis: Standard scope for a build like yours -- confirm your bid addresses it.

findings.title: Every allowance defined in writing
findings.detail: Countertops, flooring, plumbing fixtures, lighting, and appliances usually ride as allowances. A low or undefined allowance is a change order waiting to happen -- the overage is on you.
findings.basis: Standard scope for a build like yours -- confirm your bid addresses it.

findings.title: Landscaping, sod & irrigation
findings.detail: Almost always excluded or zeroed. Fine if you know it going in -- a surprise if you don't.
findings.basis: Standard scope for a build like yours -- confirm your bid addresses it.

findings.title: Insulation matches the plan spec
findings.detail: If your plans call for spray foam and the bid is priced for a batt package, the real number is different. Confirm the grade the bid actually carries.
findings.basis: Standard scope for a build like yours -- confirm your bid addresses it.

findings.title: No vague lump sums
findings.detail: A one-line "Electrical -- $35,000" with no breakdown is where change orders breed. It isn't wrong; it's unverifiable -- and unverifiable favors the builder.
findings.basis: Standard scope for a build like yours -- confirm your bid addresses it.

findings.title: Change-order pricing is in the contract
findings.detail: How overages are priced matters as much as the bid. Cost-plus-a-fixed-markup vs. re-quoted-each-time is the difference between a fair overage and a painful one.
findings.basis: Standard scope for a build like yours -- confirm your bid addresses it.

questions: What exactly does the site/allowance line cover -- clearing, driveway, and final grade -- and what happens if it runs over?
Are gutters and downspouts in the bid, and who is carrying them?
Is low-voltage / structured wiring / security in the contract as a defined line, or is it excluded?
Can you list every allowance, its dollar figure, and the exact material and square footage it buys -- in writing?
Is any landscaping, sod, or irrigation included, or is that on me?
Does the insulation line match the spec on my plans (foam vs. batt), and can I see the quote behind it?
Can the big trade lines (electrical, plumbing, HVAC) be broken into scope and allowances so I can see what's actually included?
How are change orders priced -- cost plus a fixed markup, or re-quoted each time -- and is that language in the contract?
unknowns: What's under the dirt -- rock, unsuitable soil, or drainage surprises no plan can show.
Your final selections -- a $12 tile and a $40 tile read identically on a floor plan.
Market swings between signing and dry-in -- lumber and labor move.
Permit and utility-connection fees, which vary by county and can't be verified from plans alone.
